properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 17 at 3:21PM MST until November 17 at 9:15PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Yavapai County in west central Arizona...

* Until 915 PM MST.

* At 321 PM MST, a flood wave was moving down Oak Creek from Sedona.
Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
normally dry washes, urban areas, highways, streets and
underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Cornville, Jordan, Page Springs.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Windmill Park.

This includes the following swimming holes...
Mormons Crossing.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Spring Creek, Dry Creek, Oak Creek, Turkey Creek and Verde River.
properties.instruction:
Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become
muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 9:15 PM MST. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 9:15 PM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 17 at 4:14PM MST until November 17 at 9:15PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
At 414 PM MST, a rise of 6 feet has occurred upstream of Page Springs
at Sedona, with further rises possible. Flash flooding is expected to
begin along Oak Creek in the Page Springs area within the next few
hours.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding.

SOURCE...River gauge reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of Oak Creek.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Cornville, Jordan, and Page Springs.

For Oak Creek at Cornville:
At 4:00pm the stage was 1.8 feet.
Flood Stage is 8.0 feet.
Impacts:
At 7.0 feet: Flooding begins to inundate lower terrace of RV park
upstream of Page Springs Road Bridge.

For Oak Creek at Sedona:
At 3:45pm the stage was 8.19 feet.
Flood Stage is 14.0 feet.
Impacts:
At 7.0 feet: Likely to cause minor flooding downstream in Page
Springs area near stream gage OACA3 4 to 6 hours later.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Windmill Park.

This includes the following swimming holes...
Mormons Crossing.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Verde River, Spring Creek, Oak Creek, Turkey Creek and Dry Creek.
properties.instruction:
Move to higher ground now. Act quickly to protect your life.

Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 17 at 5:20PM MST until November 17 at 9:15PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
At 520 PM MST, a rise of 6 feet has occurred upstream of Page Springs
at Sedona. The guage at Cornville has begun to rise, with a further
rise expected in the next few hours. Flash flooding is already
occurring.

Flash flooding is expected to begin along Oak Creek in the Page
Springs area within the next few hours.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding.

SOURCE...River gauge reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of Oak Creek.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Cornville, Jordan, Page Springs and Bignotti.

For Oak Creek at Cornville:
At 5:00pm the stage was 2.01 feet.
Flood Stage is 8.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 9.17 feet is expected at 9:00pm Tuesday.
Impacts:
At 7.0 feet: Flooding begins to inundate lower terrace of RV park
upstream of Page Springs Road Bridge.
At 8.0 feet: Flooding of lower terrace of RV park upstream of Page
Springs Road Bridge.
At 9.0 feet: Hiking trails along banks of creek affected. Portions of
residential yards flooded.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Windmill Park.

This includes the following swimming holes...
Mormons Crossing.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Oak Creek.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 17 at 8:14PM MST until November 17 at 9:15PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
At 814 PM MST, the river guage along Oak Creek at Cornville has risen
over 5 feet and now exceeds flood stage. Water levels are expected to
rise around another foot, before falling later tonight. Flash
flooding is already occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing flash
flooding.

SOURCE...River gauge reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of Oak Creek.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Cornville, Jordan, Page Springs and Bignotti.

For Oak Creek at Cornville:
At 8:00pm the stage was 8.24 feet.
Flood Stage is 8.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 9.17 feet is expected at 9:00pm Tuesday.
Impacts:
At 7.0 feet: Flooding begins to inundate lower terrace of RV park
upstream of Page Springs Road Bridge.
At 8.0 feet: Flooding of lower terrace of RV park upstream of Page
Springs Road Bridge.
At 9.0 feet: Hiking trails along banks of creek affected. Portions of
residential yards flooded.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Windmill Park.

This includes the following swimming holes...
Mormons Crossing.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Verde River, Spring Creek, Oak Creek, Turkey Creek and Dry Creek.
properties.instruction:
Move to higher ground now. Act quickly to protect your life.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.
